Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
options(scipen = 999)

Data

For this homework, we are going to use the Gapminder data on population (pop), GDP per capita (gdp), and life expectancy (lex). These data were downloaded and compiled using the gapminder_compile.Rmd script in the data folder.

Let’s focus our attention on data from the past 100 years, between 1925 and 2025.

gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(between(year, 1925, 2025))
  1. Use the function(s) of your choice to get an idea of the overall structure of the data, including its dimensions, column names, classes, etc.
dim(gapminder)
## [1] 19695     5
names(gapminder)
## [1] "country" "year"    "pop"     "gdp"     "lex"

  1. How many countries are represented in this dataset?
gapminder %>% 
  summarise(n_countries=n_distinct(country))#There are 195 countries in this dataset.
## # A tibble: 1 × 1
##   n_countries
##         <int>
## 1         195
  1. Which five countries have had the largest absolute population growth between 1925-2025? Show this as a table.
pop_growth <- 
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(year%in%c(1925,2025)) %>% 
  select(country,year,pop) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = pop,
              names_prefix = "pop_") %>% 
  mutate(ab_growth=pop_2025-pop_1925) %>% 
  arrange(desc(ab_growth)) %>% 
  head(n=5)#top 5 countries are india，China,Indonesia,Pakistan,USA.
names(pop_growth)
## [1] "country"   "pop_1925"  "pop_2025"  "ab_growth"
str(pop_growth)
## tibble [5 × 4] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
##  $ country  : chr [1:5] "India" "China" "Indonesia" "Pakistan" ...
##  $ pop_1925 : num [1:5] 304406019 473741473 49685263 22624808 116193761
##  $ pop_2025 : num [1:5] 1463865525 1416096094 285721236 255219554 347275807
##  $ ab_growth: num [1:5] 1159459506 942354621 236035973 232594746 231082046
  1. Make a plot that shows population growth over time for the top country you found in question #3.
india_overtime <-
  pop_growth %>% 
  arrange(desc(ab_growth)) %>% 
  head(n=1) %>% 
  pull(country)
india_overtime_data <- 
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(country==india_overtime) 
india_overtime_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year,y=pop))+
  geom_point(color="darkblue")+
  labs(title = "population growth over time for India")

  1. Has global life expectancy changed between 1925 and 2025? Show the min, median, mean, and max for all countries (combined) in the dataset.
names(gapminder)
## [1] "country" "year"    "pop"     "gdp"     "lex"
all_lex <- 
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(year%in%c(1925,2025)) %>% 
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise(min_lex=min(lex,na.rm = T),
            median_lex=median(lex,na.rm = T),
            mean_lex=mean(lex,na.rm = T),
            max_lex=max(lex,na.rm = T))
all_lex
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##    year min_lex median_lex mean_lex max_lex
##   <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1  1925    21.0       35.9     38.1    63.5
## 2  2025    52.8       74.8     73.9    85.6
  1. Make a plot that shows the distribution of life expectancy for all countries in 1925 and 2025 (try using geom_density). What do you notice about the shift in life expectancy over time?
lex_all_1925_2025 <- gapminder %>% 
  filter(year%in%c(1925,2025))
lex_all_1925_2025 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=lex,fill=factor(year)))+
  geom_density(alpha=0.6)+
  labs(title = "distribution of life expectancy with 1925 and 2025 for all countries",x="life expectancy",y="density")
## Warning: Removed 13 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_density()`).

  1. We are interested in the relationship between per capita GDP and life expectancy; i.e. does having more money help you live longer in 2025? Show this as a plot. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gdp_2025 <- 
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(year==2025,country!="Monaco")
gdp_2025 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=gdp,y=lex))+
  geom_point(alpha=0.6,color="darkblue")+
  scale_x_log10()+
  labs(title = "gdp per capita vs life expectancy in 2025")+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",se=F)#higher gdp thend to have higher life expectancy.
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Which five countries have had the highest absolute GDP per capita growth over the past 50 years? Show this as a table. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gdp_growth <- 
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(year%in%c(1975,2025),country!="Monaco") %>% 
  select(country,year,gdp) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = gdp,
              names_prefix = "gdp_")
gdp_growth
## # A tibble: 194 × 3
##    country             gdp_1975 gdp_2025
##    <chr>                  <dbl>    <dbl>
##  1 Afghanistan            2228.    2093.
##  2 Angola                 4131.    7457.
##  3 Albania                4249.   20362.
##  4 Andorra               52278.   67385.
##  5 UAE                   74397.   72660.
##  6 Argentina             15711.   28467.
##  7 Armenia                8890.   21539.
##  8 Antigua and Barbuda    7466.   30871.
##  9 Australia             22732.   61943.
## 10 Austria               22384.   64665.
## # ℹ 184 more rows
top5_growth_gdp <- gdp_growth %>% 
  mutate(gdp_1975_2025=gdp_2025-gdp_1975) %>% 
  arrange(desc(gdp_1975_2025)) %>% 
  head(n=5)
top5_growth_gdp#top 5 are Singapore,Ireland,Luxembourg,Guyana,Norway.
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country    gdp_1975 gdp_2025 gdp_1975_2025
##   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>         <dbl>
## 1 Singapore    12896.  137906.       125010.
## 2 Ireland      14336.  119406.       105071.
## 3 Luxembourg   30950.  131038.       100088.
## 4 Guyana        5071.   79371.        74300.
## 5 Norway       25513.   94896.        69382.
  1. How does per capita GDP growth compare between these same five countries over the past 50 years? Show this as a plot.
top5_growth <- top5_growth_gdp$country
top5_growth_time <- 
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(year>=1975,country%in%top5_growth)
top5_growth_time %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year,y=gdp,color=country))+
  geom_line(size=1)+
  scale_y_log10()+
  labs(title = "gdp per capita growth for top 5 in past 50 years")

  1. Do one analysis of your choice that includes a table and plot as outputs.#show the 5 lowest countries with its gdp growth from 1975 to 2025
gdp_growth_low  <-  
  gapminder %>% 
  filter(year%in%c(1975,2025),country!="Monaco") %>% 
  select(year,country,gdp) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = gdp,
              names_prefix = "low_") %>% 
  mutate(gdp_growth_low_num=low_2025-low_1975)
gdp_growth_low_5 <- 
  gdp_growth_low%>% 
  arrange(gdp_growth_low_num) %>% 
  head(n=5)
gdp_growth_low_5 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=country,y=gdp_growth_low_num))+
  geom_point(color="darkblue")+
  labs(title = "Bottom 5 countries with their gdp from 1975-2025")
